attestations.source_text: The passé simple (simple past, historical past) is a verb tense used mainly in written French, for literary and historical material. It may also be heard during a formal speech. It is the equivalent of the passé composé, used to recount a specific action in the past.

sections.title: Formation of the passé simple: regular -er verbs

attestations.section_title: Formation of the passé simple: regular -er verbs
attestations.source_text: The passé simple of regular -er verbs is formed by adding the endings -ai, -as, -a, -âmes, -âtes, -èrent to the infinitive stem.
Verbs like commencer and manger have a spelling change. When the passé simple ending starts with -a, use the cedilla (ç) for verbs ending in -cer and add an extra -e- for verbs ending in -ger.

sections.title: Formation of the passé simple: regular -ir and -re verbs

attestations.section_title: Formation of the passé simple: regular -ir and -re verbs
attestations.source_text: The passé simple of regular -ir and -re verbs like partir (to leave) and répondre (to answer) is formed by adding the endings -is, -is, -it, -îmes, -îtes, -irent to the infinitive stem.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Formation of passé simple for regular -er verbs
grammar_rules.summary: Add endings -ai, -as, -a, -âmes, -âtes, -èrent to the infinitive stem.
grammar_rules.explanation: The passé simple of regular -er verbs is formed by adding specific endings to the infinitive stem.
usage: Used in written and formal French to express completed past actions.
exceptions: Verbs ending in -cer and -ger have spelling changes before endings starting with -a.
common_traps: Do not forget the circumflex on -âmes and -âtes endings.

study.frequency_note: Common in written French and literature.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Spelling changes for -cer and -ger verbs in passé simple
grammar_rules.summary: Use cedilla (ç) for -cer verbs and add extra -e- for -ger verbs when ending starts with -a.
grammar_rules.explanation: When the passé simple ending starts with -a, verbs ending in -cer use a cedilla and verbs ending in -ger add an extra -e- before the ending.
usage: Applies to all forms with endings beginning with -a: -a, -âmes, -âtes, -èrent.
common_traps: Forgetting the cedilla or the extra -e-.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Avoir and être are irregular in the passé simple
grammar_rules.summary: Avoir and être have irregular stems and endings in the passé simple.
grammar_rules.explanation: Avoir uses stem eu- and être uses stem fu- in the passé simple.
grammar_rules.formation: avoir: eus, eus, eut, eûmes, eûtes, eurent; être: fus, fus, fut, fûmes, fûtes, furent
usage: Common in literature and formal writing.
common_traps: Do not confuse eu- and fu- forms.

grammar_rules.explanation: Irregular verbs have unpredictable passé simple forms; sometimes the stem resembles the past participle.

exceptions: Not a fixed rule; many irregular stems must be memorized.
common_traps: Assuming regularity based on past participle.
